archetype: Azorius draw-go control with one alternate-win finisher. The audit's `combo` label is a keyword artifact, not a reading: deck_audit.detect_archetype scans strategic_frame.json's free prose for hints in a fixed order and tests `combo` before `control`, so it matched the frame's sentence 'there is no two-card combo' rather than the frame's opening words, 'Azorius draw-go control that gifts the whole table cards'. bracket-check, recomputed today, reports two_card_infinites [] and one contained line — Approach of the Second Sun + Mystical Tutor — which is not infinite. The label is not cosmetic: it applied the combo budget's tutors 4-8 and protection 4-6, which this deck sits inside at 4 and 5, and withheld the control budget, under which mana-base reads 37-39 rather than 36-38 and sweepers reads 5-7 rather than 1-3. Re-run under `--archetype control`, exactly one axis changes VERDICT: sweepers, 'at' against the interaction suite's cap of 1-3 and 'under' against control's 5-7. mana-base is 'under' either way and goes from three short to four; interaction is 'at' under both (14, against a floor of 8 or a band of 12-15); protection is 'at' under both; tutors loses its band and becomes informational.
verdict: This deck owns the long game and cannot close it. Over 120 Forge games it placed first 16 times and second 43 times of 94 ranked games, mean position 2.319, and won 0.252 (ci95 [0.180, 0.342], n=120) against a table null of 0.144 — the record of a deck that outlives the pod and then runs out of ways to end it. What binds is access to the card that ends it, not survival: 20 of the 27 wins were Approach, five cards in the 99 search a library and two can name a seven-mana sorcery, and that three-card group is drawn in 0.495 of goldfish games and 0.361 by turn six. Mana is the same bottleneck's second half and ranks below it, because a game in which Approach was never drawn cannot be fixed with a land.

engine.declared: Give the whole table cards, convert that gift into a one-sided discount, draw and Treasure, buy turns behind a fort, and cast Approach of the Second Sun twice.

components.reading: The most reliable thing the deck does: assembled 0.92, 0.828 by turn six, mean turn 2.461. Eleven deep is well past the point the redundancy table stops paying, and four of the eleven — Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Kami of the Crescent Moon and Dictate of Kruphix — fire only 'at the beginning of each player's draw step', so they hand a card to whichever seat is untapping, not to a discount on your own main phase.

Heliod plus the mana to flip him: 0.823 assembled, 0.642 by turn six, mean turn 4.808. Commander-gated, and Forge resolved Heliod in 0.567 of 120 games with 0.69 casts a game, so this component's real availability at a table is lower than the model's.
The conversion layer that makes a symmetric gift one-sided: 0.787 assembled, 0.581 by turn six. Seven deep, and the redundancy table prices a seven-of at 41% of openers, which is what this is.

The thinnest group in the file at two cards: 0.366 assembled, 0.256 by turn six. It is thin and it is also not on the win route — the seat's noncombat damage over 120 games was mean 1.68, median 0.0, and the three hand-size punishers this pair used to sit beside were cut on exactly that evidence.

The group that gates the deck's actual win, and the one this diagnosis is about: 0.495 assembled, 0.361 by turn six, mean turn 4.015. It gates the FIRST cast only — Approach's own text puts it seventh from the top on resolution, so the second copy arrives on its own within seven draws.
Held interaction: 0.843 assembled, 0.707 by turn six, mean turn 3.001. Holding it and paying for it are different problems — castable is 0.626 at turn six against 0.927 in hand.

Commander insurance: 0.680 assembled, 0.526 by turn six. Leyline of Anticipation is the member that does not read the commander, which matters because the flash grant is what lets the discount be spent at all.
A body that can block a flier: 0.750 assembled, 0.604 by turn six. Kefnet cannot block below seven cards in hand, so the group is five unconditional blockers and one conditional one.

The fort: 0.487 assembled, 0.355 by turn six — the least reliable of the four defensive groups, against 0.680, 0.750 and 0.843 for the other three. Its thinness is cushioned by those three in a way the win route's is not.

The X-spell mana sinks, 0.790 assembled and 0.673 by turn six. Whether the commander's discount lets you choose a larger X is unsettled and is the whole justification for this group; it is in open_questions.

cut_candidates.why: Four mana to give each opponent two extra cards in their own draw step. Against three opponents that is six cards a round to the table and two to you, and the deck's measured death is an opponent's board: eliminated in 74 of 120 games, 53 attributed, all of them as damage, 39 of those to one seat whose threats fly. Enumerated across all eleven ignition permanents by oracle text, it hands opponents more cards per round at a fixed rate than any other: Howling Mine, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Dictate of Kruphix and Scrawling Crawler give three; Temple Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain and The Second Doctor give at most three and only when you spend a tap or the opponent accepts; Loran gives one; and Forced Fruition gives none at a fixed rate at all, being seven per opponent spell. The gift group is eleven deep and assembles in 0.92 of games; it can afford to lose its most generous member.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: This is the deck's thesis at its loudest, and the honest price is high: two extra cards a round for you, a standing {2} discount on every opponent's turn under the flash grant, and the largest fixed feed for Consecrated Sphinx, Smothering Tithe, Faerie Mastermind and Scrawling Crawler. The corpus has no section on symmetrical resource gifts, so nothing on disk can tell you where this trade turns net-positive — that is in open_questions, and until it is answered this cut is a judgement rather than a finding.

open_questions.question: Can the second Approach of the Second Sun be cast at an opponent's end step under Heliod, the Warped Eclipse's flash grant or Leyline of Anticipation, and is Fierce Guardianship's alternative cost live in that window when Heliod is the commander on the battlefield?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Stack 002 settles the sorcery-speed cast on your own turn and nothing else. The end-step cast spends the table's responses first, which is the whole pivot; and the free-counter backup depends on Heliod being there, which Forge measured at 0.567 of 120 games. If the end-step window is legal, the pilot's commit turn changes and the protection package is priced differently.

open_questions.question: Does Heliod, the Warped Eclipse's cost reduction let you choose a larger X on Braingeyser, Stroke of Genius, Prosperity, Skyscribing, Mathemagics, Secure the Wastes, Walking Ballista, Hangarback Walker or Mikaeus, the Lunarch — and is X chosen before or after the reduction applies?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The eight-card X-spell component assembles 0.790 and its entire justification is this interaction. Two of this document's cuts come out of that group, and if X is chosen after the reduction the group is worth more than it is priced at here.

open_questions.question: While Lightning Greaves is equipped to Heliod, can Karametra's Blessing or Guardian of Faith's enters trigger still target him, and can the Greaves be moved off in response?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Greaves grants shroud, which stops your own targeting, and equip is sorcery-speed. If two of the five commander-insurance slots are mutually exclusive with a third while equipped, the 0.680 assembly figure overstates what the pilot can actually do in the removal window — and that package is the whole of v1.1.0.

open_questions.question: When is a symmetrical resource gift net-positive? Specifically: how many converters does a deck need before handing three opponents N cards a round is better than not, and how does the answer change against an aggressive seat?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This decides the Font of Mythos cut, which is the painful one in this document and the one whose case rests on a judgement about symmetry rather than on a figure. strategic_frame.json's own gaps list records that the corpus has no section on symmetrical gifts at all, so nothing on disk can adjudicate it.

open_questions.question: How many tutor and protection slots is a single 'you win the game' card worth in a four-player pod, and how should the one-window cast be timed against three potential responders?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The two tutor adds in this document are sized against the redundancy table, which is about effect classes rather than about a card that ends the game. The frame records that querying the corpus for alternate win conditions returns 0.407 and nothing on topic, so this deck's entire plan has no home in the doc.

open_questions.question: Can goldfish_targets express the deck's actual win — Approach in hand AND seven mana available on two separate turns — or must the gap be recorded rather than modelled?
open_questions.why_it_matters: 'Win condition access' at 0.495 measures drawing one of three cards and nothing prices whether the deck can pay {6}{W} twice. Mean available mana crosses 7 between turn 8 (6.966) and turn 9 (7.612) with the commander's discount switched off in the model, so the cost side of the deck's only win is currently unmeasured.

gaps: EVERY FORGE FIGURE IN THIS DOCUMENT DESCRIBES A DIFFERENT DECK. The 120-game run's heliod seat carries decklist_sha256 decc32b080fe — v1.0.0 — and the run record says so itself. `deck-version show v1.0.0` gives the diff as -10 +10: nine nonbasic cards out, nine in, plus five Islands rebalanced to Plains. All nine of the added nonbasics — Angelic Wall, Archangel of Tithes, Drift of Phantasms, Ghostly Prison, Guardian of Faith, Karametra's Blessing, Kefnet the Mindful, Leyline of Anticipation and Lightning Greaves — sit in the fort, the flier-blocker group or the commander-insurance package, which is to say the run cannot see any of the deck's answer to what killed it. deck_versions.json's `paper` lock still points at decc32b080fe, so the measured list is the SLEEVED one and the current 99 is an unsleeved proposal. `simulate heliod --vs giada-angels --vs baylen-tokens --vs abaddon` on 214af3084f80 is the highest-value measurement this deck is missing, and no routing value in open_questions covers a Forge re-run.

The commander-removal decomposition that justified v1.1.0 — '45% removal rate', 119 measured departures, the mass/targeted split and the exile share — is NOT ON DISK in this deck's artifacts. engine.json says so explicitly and repeats it as the version's claim rather than as a measurement. The two places it survives disagree: poh_procedures.json says 33 of 119 departures were to exile in one note and 57 mass against 41 targeted in another, while the brief that commissioned this diagnosis says 21 of 119 to exile. Nothing here can adjudicate that, and no axis in this document rests on it.

strategic_frame.json quotes goldfish component figures that goldfish_metrics.json no longer holds (0.935 against 0.920 for the table draw engine, 0.334 against 0.328 for engine-plus-drain, 0.679 against 0.495 for win-condition access), because three membership corrections have landed since it was written. engine.json's open_questions[3] also still carries 0.596 for win-condition access. This document uses goldfish_metrics.json throughout, via deck-audit.

bracket_report.json carries no `decklist_sha256`, so deck-audit's freshness block reports it as neither current nor stale.
